clue.text: Senior officer found with drug in empty shed is investigated

indicators.note: the officer and drug are placed in the emptied shed
an empty shed has lost its contents, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: a cop is a police officer, here dressed up as senior
E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A top policeman with drugs turns up in a shed that is being searched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word; the definition is the past participle alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To scope something out is to examine or look into it, so scoped is a synonym of investigated.

clue.text: Stop king and fool becoming bound together

parts.note: to close something is to stop or end it
K is the chess abbreviation for king
nit is short for nitwit, a fool

explanation.surface: Ending a monarch and jester's partnership makes them inseparable.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-knit group is tightly united, as if tied to each other.

clue.text: Verbose professional listened to short musical phrases

parts.note: pro is short for professional

indicators.note: listened to means the phrase is heard, so the letters entered sound like it

parts.note: licks are short phrases played by jazz or rock musicians

explanation.surface: A wordy expert listens to snippets of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolix means using too many words, a synonym of wordy.

clue.text: Specify putting giants' pants in river

indicators.note: the jumbled word is placed in the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

indicators.note: pants as slang means rubbish or badly made, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Instructions to put the big men's trousers in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers, but it is British slang for rubbish, so it signals an anagram. The Dee is a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: To designate is to name or indicate formally, which is to specify.

clue.text: New price includes chemist's third formula

indicators.note: the rearranged price takes the extra letter inside it
a new version of the word price has its letters rearranged
the third letter of chemist is wanted, counting from its start

explanation.surface: A fresh price at the pharmacy covers a formula.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set formula of ingredients and method, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Bishop adopting star competitor

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the bishop's letters enclose the star

parts.note: RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title
an ace is a star performer

explanation.surface: A churchman takes on a top competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is someone who competes in races.

clue.text: Put in an appearance outside retro car plant

indicators.note: outside means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to come is to put in an appearance, past tense came

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the car's letters run in reverse

parts.note: a limo is a limousine, a car

explanation.surface: Attending a gathering around an old-fashioned motor and a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory, but it is the herb; 'retro' turns LIMO into OMIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Camomile is a daisy-like herb, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Short coat given to old philosopher

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to plate is to coat with metal

explanation.surface: A brief jacket is handed to an ancient thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' looks like a garment but is the verb, to plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Greek philosopher, student of Socrates.

clue.text: Passionate Australian given another room with American

indicators.note: another version of the word room has its letters rearranged

parts.note: US stands for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: An ardent Aussie is given a new room alongside an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorous means full of romantic or sexual desire, which is passion.

clue.text: Herbicide makes a chap a goner, unfortunately

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a chap

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A weedkiller dooms a man, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link word. The blog notes the defoliant was used in Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a defoliant sprayed in the Vietnam War, a kind of herbicide.

clue.text: Firm agreement

definitions.meaning: a pact or treaty between parties

explanation.definitionFit: Compact as adjective means dense or firm; as noun it means a formal agreement.

clue.text: Troy's first prophet turned up to encourage woodworker

indicators.note: first picks the initial letter of Troy's
turned up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, reversing the word

parts.note: a seer is a prophet
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A Trojan seer upends himself to spur on a carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woodworker' suggests a carpenter, but is a playful definition of someone who works on trees. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree surgeon works on living trees, so wood is the material of the trade.

clue.text: Regimen is proven to regenerate flower

indicators.note: regenerating the words remakes them, so their letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A health regime is shown to renew a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a plant with yellow blooms that open in the evening, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Play bagging nation's first award for excellence on Broadway

indicators.note: bagging means holding inside, so the toy takes the letter within it

parts.note: a toy is a plaything; play as a verb also means toy with

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of nation's

explanation.surface: A drama wins the country's top theatre prize in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tony Awards honour achievement in New York theatre, so a Tony is such an award.

clue.text: People injured by throwaway garments?

parts.note: a throwaway remark is a casual one
ties are garments worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Victims of a disaster are pictured as offhand pieces of neckwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical reading of the second half: offhand neckties.
explanation.definitionFit: Casualties are those hurt or killed in an accident or battle.

clue.text: Without cover, nudes ruin broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Naked models are exposed when their ruin goes on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without insurance cover means having no protection against loss.

clue.text: Fancy popular gallery having racist leader in charge!

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the gallery has the other letters held within it

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of racist

explanation.surface: A popular gallery shows a bigoted figure at the helm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornate, which intricate also means.

clue.text: Various roads set out

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Several streets are laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted means of different kinds, a synonym of various.

clue.text: Place where meat gets cooked in mould is beside small lake

indicators.note: beside places one piece next to the other in a row

parts.note: rot is decay or mould
taken as written
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Meat is roasted in a mouldy spot by a little lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a restaurant or device that roasts meat on a turning spit.

clue.text: Commotion caused by heads of state talking in riddles

indicators.note: the heads of the words are their initial letters

explanation.surface: Turmoil stirred up by leaders who speak in puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a fuss or commotion, a synonym.

clue.text: Brother returned short letter to person from Brest

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the note is read in reverse

parts.note: a note is a short letter

explanation.surface: A sibling sends back a brief message to a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like a cut but is part of the definition of NOTE. Brest is a port in Brittany.
explanation.definitionFit: Brest is in Brittany, so a native of it is a Breton.

annotationWithheld.clue: Alien contrives to secure a spell in the military

clue.text: Sign made by team leader at sporting event

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a race is a sporting event

explanation.surface: A signal from the captain at a sports meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is a mark or sign left behind.

clue.text: Dared tangle with a snake!

indicators.note: tangling the word twists its letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a serpent for a dare.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is the common European viper, an example of a snake.

clue.text: Revered former editor pinching a large journalist's bottom

indicators.note: pinching means nabbing, so the former editor holds the other letters inside

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the bottom of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A respected ex-editor steals a sizeable sum from a reporter's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Exalted means held in high regard or honoured, close to revered.

clue.text: Retiring Queen and followers prepare for alternative employment

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the abbreviation for queen is turned round

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
a train is a retinue of followers

explanation.surface: A monarch stepping down with her entourage gets ready for a new career.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrain is to learn new skills so as to take up a different job.

clue.text: Heavy drinking session sees new head of department drowning in ale

indicators.note: the new head is drowning in the ale, so it sits inside the drink's letters

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A binge sees the new department boss submerged in beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bender is slang for a drinking spree.

clue.text: Revolutionary coming back to eat pub grub?

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the turned-round red swallows the pub
coming back means going in reverse, so the word red is read backwards

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary communist
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A returning radical heads for the pub for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pub grub' reads as one phrase, but only 'grub' is the definition; the pub belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is informal for food, and dinner is the main meal.
